config.title: Build stale while revalidate cache layer

intro.title: Build stale while revalidate cache layer
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple 'stale-while-revalidate' (SWR) cache layer in JavaScript. This pattern allows your application to show cached data immediately while fetching fresh data in the background, improving perceived performance. You will learn to implement this using core JavaScript constructs like objects for caching, async/await for handling promises, and Date objects for tracking cache age. By the end, you'll have a reusable cache function that intelligently manages data freshness and updates.
intro.usecase: This stale-while-revalidate pattern is essential for building responsive data dashboards and financial applications where users need immediate access to cached data while fresh information loads in the background. Product examples include real-time analytics dashboards that show cached metrics while fetching updated numbers, or e-commerce product listings that display cached prices while checking for current inventory. Developers implement this to prevent loading spinners during every data refresh, creating smoother user experiences in applications like social media feeds, weather apps, and stock trading platforms where both speed and accuracy matter.

objectives: Implement a basic cache storage mechanism using JavaScript objects
Construct a function that checks for stale cache entries based on timestamps
Configure a revalidation process that updates cached data asynchronously
Integrate cache retrieval with fallback to fresh data fetching
Manipulate cache state to handle concurrent requests efficiently
Initialize a cache layer with configurable stale time thresholds
Apply the stale-while-revalidate pattern to optimize data fetching in a sample application

steps.instruction: Create a new JavaScript file and import the required dependencies for building a cache layer with stale-while-revalidate functionality.

steps.hint: Use the class keyword followed by the class name. Inside the constructor, set this.store to an empty object.

// Import the required dependencies here

steps.title: Add cache storage initialization
steps.instruction: Inside the Cache class constructor, initialize a Map object to store cache entries.
steps.hint: Add a line in the constructor that creates a new Map and assigns it to a property, such as this.cache = new Map().
steps.expectedOutcome: The Cache class constructor now has a Map property ready to store cache entries.
successCriteria: A Map object is initialized and assigned to a property (e.g., this.cache) inside the Cache constructor.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Implement the get method
steps.instruction: Inside the Cache class, add a get method that takes a key parameter and returns the cached value for that key.
steps.hint: Define a method named get with one parameter. Inside the method, return the value from the cache storage using the key.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Cache class will have a get method that retrieves cached data by key.
successCriteria: The Cache class contains a get method with a key parameter that returns the cached value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but make sure it's named 'get', takes a key parameter, and returns the cached value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The get method is not properly implemented. Check that you've defined a method named 'get' with a key parameter that returns the cached value.

steps.title: Add stale-while-revalidate logic to get method
steps.instruction: Inside the get method, add logic to check if cached data is stale and trigger revalidation while returning stale data.
steps.hint: You'll need to check the current time against the cache entry's timestamp to determine staleness. If stale, trigger a background fetch but still return the cached data.
steps.expectedOutcome: The get method will now check for stale data and trigger revalidation while immediately returning cached data.
successCriteria: The get method includes logic to check staleness based on timestamp, triggers revalidation for stale data, and returns cached data immediately.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some logic, but make sure to check the timestamp for staleness and trigger revalidation while still returning cached data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The get method doesn't yet implement stale-while-revalidate logic. Review the pattern and try again.

steps.title: Implement the set method
steps.instruction: Add a set method to the Cache class that stores data with a timestamp and metadata for tracking freshness.
steps.hint: The set method should take a key and value, then store them in the cache storage along with a timestamp and metadata object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Cache class now has a set method that can store data with freshness tracking metadata.
successCriteria: The set method is defined in the Cache class and stores data with a timestamp and metadata object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your set method stores the data with both a timestamp and metadata object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The set method is missing or doesn't properly store data with timestamp and metadata. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Add revalidation method
steps.instruction: Inside the Cache class, add a method named 'revalidate' that takes a key parameter and returns a promise that fetches fresh data and updates the cache with it.
steps.hint: The method should be async and use fetch to get new data, then call the set method to update the cache.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Cache class now has a revalidate method that handles fetching fresh data and updating the cache.
successCriteria: The Cache class includes an async revalidate method that takes a key, fetches fresh data, and updates the cache using the set method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a revalidate method, but make sure it's async, fetches fresh data, and calls set to update the cache.
steps.feedbackWrong: The revalidate method is missing or doesn't correctly fetch and update the cache. Review the stale-while-revalidate concept.

steps.title: Add cache statistics tracking
steps.instruction: Inside the Cache class constructor, add properties to track cache hits, misses, and revalidations. Initialize them to 0.
steps.hint: Add properties like this.hits, this.misses, and this.revalidations in the constructor and set them to 0.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Cache class constructor will have three new properties (hits, misses, revalidations) initialized to 0 for tracking cache performance.
successCriteria: The Cache constructor contains this.hits = 0, this.misses = 0, and this.revalidations = 0 properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some statistics properties, but make sure to include all three: hits, misses, and revalidations, all initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The statistics tracking properties weren't added correctly. Add this.hits, this.misses, and this.revalidations in the constructor and set them to 0.
